name: Sterling-Nakamura Diplomatic Protocol AI
description: An AI system that manages complex multi-party negotiations by modeling each participant's interests, constraints, cultural background, and psychological profile to identify optimal compromise positions. The DPAI conducts real-time analysis of negotiation dynamics — speech patterns, micro-expressions, biometric stress indicators — and provides its user with recommended responses, predicted counterparty reactions, and identified deal-breaking triggers. Sterling-Nakamura deploys it in every significant negotiation, giving their representatives an information advantage that borders on mind-reading.
social_impact: DPAI has made negotiating with Sterling-Nakamura an exercise in asymmetric information warfare — their negotiators know what you want, what you will accept, and what will make you walk away, while you are negotiating blind. The technology has given Sterling-Nakamura a structural advantage in every deal they make, and counterparties have learned to demand AI-free negotiation protocols — demands that Sterling-Nakamura agrees to while running DPAI through their neural interface anyway.
story_hooks: A DPAI analysis of a negotiation counterpart revealed that they are not the decision-maker they claim to be — their stress patterns indicate they are acting under coercion from an unidentified party.
Two DPAI-assisted negotiators from opposing corporations have discovered that their AIs are converging on the same compromise — the question is whether the deal serves the corporations or the AIs.
